({{IPA|de|ˈhaːpak ˌlɔɪ̯t}}) is a German international shipping and container [[transportation company]], the 5th-largest in the world by total [[Twenty-foot equivalent unit|TEU]] capacity.{{Cite web |title=PublicTop100 |url=https://alphaliner.axsmarine.com/PublicTop100/ |access-date=2025-07-19 |website=alphaliner.axsmarine.com |archive-date=19 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819163231/https://alphaliner.axsmarine.com/PublicTop100/ |url-status=live }} It was formed in 1970 through a merger of two German maritime transportation companies.{{cite web |url=http://www.castlesoftheseas.nl/hapag-lloyd-2.html |title=Hapag-Lloyd |publisher=Castles of the Seas |access-date=22 September 2019 |archive-date=18 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200218102806/http://www.castlesoftheseas.nl/hapag-lloyd-2.html |url-status=live}} [[File:Hapag-Lloyd shipping container.jpeg|thumb|Hapag-Lloyd container]] ==History== The company was formed on 1 September 1970, by the merger of [[Hamburg America Line|Hamburg-American Line (HAPAG)]], founded in 1847, and [[Norddeutscher Lloyd]] (known in English as North German Lloyd), which was formed in 1857. Since its formation, Hapag-Lloyd has seen changes among its shareholders and has also undergone a number of mergers with other companies. For instance, Hapag-Lloyd was completely acquired by, and became a [[subsidiary]] of [[TUI AG]] ([[Hanover]]) in 1998. This transition was followed by TUI selling a majority stake of Hapag-Lloyd to private investors in Hamburg in 2009 and further sales in 2012. Other important events in the history of the company include Hapag-Lloyd's acquisition of [[CP Ships]] in 2005 as well as Hapag-Lloyd's merger with the container business of [[CSAV]] in 2014, and United Arab Shipping Company in 2017. ===HAPAG=== {{Main|Hamburg America Line}} [[File:Hapag-Lloyd.jpg|thumb|right|Headquarters of Hapag-Lloyd in Hamburg]] The [[Hamburg America Line|'''H'''amburg-'''A'''merikanische '''P'''acketfahrt-'''Ac'''tien-'''G'''esellschaft]] for shipping across the [[Atlantic Ocean]] was founded in Hamburg. In 1912, HAPAG built the first of their "Big Three" ocean liners; the ''[[SS Imperator|Imperator]]'', followed by its twin ''[[SS Leviathan|Vaterland]]''. A third ship, ''[[SS Bismarck|Bismarck]]'', was under construction at the outbreak of [[World War I]] and was completed after the war for [[White Star Line]] as the [[RMS Majestic (1914)|''Majestic'']]. These were the first liners to exceed 50,000 gross register tons and 900 feet (274 m) in length. During [[World War I]], the majority of HAPAG's fleet of 175 ships were wiped out, and most of the surviving ships (including the "Big Three") had to be turned over to the winning side as war reparations. After the war's end, HAPAG rebuilt its fleet with much smaller ships than before the war.{{cite web |url=http://www.theshipslist.com/ships/lines/hamburg.html |title=Hamburg America Line |publisher=Ships List |access-date=22 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525231134/http://www.theshipslist.com/ships/lines/hamburg.html |archive-date=2011-05-25}} {{See also|1900 Hoboken Docks Fire|Albert Ballin}} ===Norddeutscher Lloyd=== {{Main|Norddeutscher Lloyd}} {{See also|1900 Hoboken Docks fire}} [[File:Kaiser-wilhelm-II liner.jpg|thumb|right|The NDL liner ''Kaiser Wilhelm II'', which made its maiden voyage in 1903]] [[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 102-09397, Bremerhaven, Schiffe "Europa" und "Bremen".jpg|thumb|right|Flagships of North German Lloyd – ''[[SS Bremen (1928)|Bremen]]'' and ''[[SS Europa (1928)|Europa]]'']] [[Norddeutscher Lloyd]] (NDL) was formed in 1857 in the City-State of [[Bremen (city)|Bremen]], offering passenger and cargo transportation between Bremen and New York, with an emphasis on emigration to the United States. Service started in June 1858 with the ''Bremen'', the first of four steamships,{{Cite book |title=Die Seeschiffe des Norddeutschen Lloyd 1857 bis 1919, Vol. 1 |last=Kludas |first=Arnold |year=1991 |location=Herford |pages=10}} and the company established its American base at [[Hoboken, New Jersey]]. NDL eventually built a large fleet of ships that carried many thousands of emigrants westwards, with around 218,000 passengers transported across the Atlantic in 1913 alone.{{Cite book |last=Drechsel |first=Edwin |title=Norddeutscher Lloyd Bremen 1857–1970: History, Fleet, Ship Mails |publisher=Cordillera Pub. Co. |year=1994 |volume=I |location=Vancouver |pages=410}} The outbreak of [[World War I]] resulted in the internment of 32 vessels in US ports, a status later changed to confiscation when the US entered the war in 1917.{{Cite book |last=Drechsel |first=Edwin |title=Norddeutscher Lloyd Bremen 1857–1970: History, Fleet, Ship Mails |publisher=Cordillera Pub. Co. |year=1994 |volume=II |location=Vancouver |page=1}} Likewise, its Hoboken base was confiscated and turned over to the US Navy, which used it as a transshipping point for the duration of the war.{{cite book |author=Kenneth T. Jackson |year=1995 |title=The Encyclopedia of New York City |publisher=New-York Historical Society; Yale University Press |page=854}} As with HAPAG, the NDL ships surviving the war were eventually confiscated as reparation, leaving the company to start over from scratch. US operations were resumed in 1922, when NDL was able to purchase its former base from the United States Alien Property Administrator.{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}} NDL took delivery of new liners ''[[SS Bremen (1928)|Bremen]]'' and ''[[SS Liberte|Europa]]'' in 1929–30.{{Cite book |last=Kludas |first=Arnold |title=Die Seeschiffe des Norddeutschen Lloyd 1920 bis 1970 |publisher=Koehlers Verlagsgesellschaft mbH |year=1992 |isbn=3-7822-0534-0 |location=Herford |pages=84–85}} During [[World War II]], NDL repeated its World War I experience, with some parts of its fleet again being interned at the outbreak of the war, while a number of vessels remained under NDL control.NDL Annual Report 1939–1948. p. 4. One such exception was the ''Bremen'', which raced across the Atlantic, and achieved protection at [[Murmansk]] in 1939, before eventually making a dash for Bremerhaven, where she was ultimately destroyed by a fire in 1941.{{Cite book |last=Huchthausen |first=Peter A. |date=2005 |title=Shadow Voyage: The Extraordinary Wartime Escape of the Legendary SS Bremen |location=Hoboken, N.J. |publisher=J. Wiley & Sons |isbn=0-471-45758-2 |oclc=55764562}} Passenger service resumed in 1954 with the ''Gripsholm'' formerly belonging to the ''[[Swedish American Line]]'' (the ship was renamed to {{MS|Berlin|1925|6}} only the following year).{{Cite book |last=Drechsel |first=Edwin |title=Norddeutscher Lloyd |year=1995 |volume=II |location=Vancouver |pages=493}} Later two other second-hand ships, {{SS|Bremen|1957|6}} (formerly ''Pasteur'') and {{MS|Europa|1953|6}} (formerly Swedish American Line's ''Kungsholm''), were purchased. NDL attained several speed records over the years. Notable among them was the record for the run between [[Southampton]] and [[New York, New York|New York]] of eight days in 1881, which was set by the ''Elbe''; and the record for the fastest transatlantic crossing set by the new ''Bremen'' in 1929 (see [[Blue Riband]]). ===Hapag-Lloyd=== [[File:Osaka Express, at the Amazone harbour, Port of Rotterdam, Holland 14-Jul-2007.jpg|thumb|''Osaka Express'' at Port of Rotterdam]] Hapag and NDL continued to compete until they established a joint-venture container line. The "Hapag-Lloyd Container Line", founded in 1967 and operating from 1968 onward, was established to share the huge investments related to the containerisation of the fleets. The two companies finally merged on 1 September 1970, under the name Hapag-Lloyd. Hapag-Lloyd was acquired in 1998 by Preussag AG (since 2002 named [[TUI AG]] ([[Hanover]])), a tourism conglomerate, and became its fully owned subsidiary in 2002.[http://www.arabiansupplychain.com/article-11095-hapag-lloyd-ceo-reduction-in-operational-costs-needed/ "Hapag-Lloyd CEO: reduction in operational costs needed"] ({{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629082849/http://www.arabiansupplychain.com/article-11095-hapag-lloyd-ceo-reduction-in-operational-costs-needed/ |date=29 June 2017 }}), Arabian Supply Chain, 30 March 2015. Accessed 23 July 2015. In August 2008, TUI announced an intention to sell its entire stake in Hapag-Lloyd shipping activities before the end of that year. The Terminal & Infrastructure division has been operating under the brand name "Hanseatic Global Terminals" since July 2024. It is a fully owned but independent stand-alone business unit based in Rotterdam.{{Cite web |date=2024-07-01 |title=Hanseatic Global Terminals: A new brand to strengthen and expand the terminal business |url=https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2024/07/hanseatic-global-terminals--a-new-brand-to-strengthen-and-expand.html |access-date=2024-12-11}} Also in 2023, Hapag-Lloyd and the Brazilian shipping and waterway logistics company Norsul set up a new joint venture called "Norcoast". Based on a 50-50 partnership, Norcoast started offering container cabotage and feeder services in Brazilian ports in the first quarter of 2024.[https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2023/10/hapag-lloyd-and-norsul-to-launch-new-joint-venture-company-for-c.html Hapag-Lloyd and Norsul to launch new joint venture company for cabotage business in Brazil.] Retrieved 22 November 2023. In January 2024, it was announced that Hapag-Lloyd, together with [[Maersk]], would launch a long-term operational cooperation under the name [[Gemini Cooperation]] in February 2025; Hapag-Lloyd simultaneously announced that it would leave “THE Alliance” in January 2025.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-17 |title=Maersk und Hapag-Lloyd vereinbaren gemeinsame operative Zusammenarbeit - Hapag-Lloyd |url=https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/de/company/press/releases/2024/01/maersk-and-hapag-lloyd-are-entering-into-an-operational-cooperat.html |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=www.hapag-lloyd.com |language=de |archive-date=12 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212103047/https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/de/company/press/releases/2024/01/maersk-and-hapag-lloyd-are-entering-into-an-operational-cooperat.html |url-status=live }} The new cooperation is expected to comprise around 340 ships with a combined capacity of 3.7 million standard containers (TEU); of these, Maersk is to provide 60% and Hapag-Lloyd 40%.{{Cite web |title=Gemini Cooperation - Hapag-Lloyd |url=https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/de/services-information/gemini-cooperation.html |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=www.hapag-lloyd.com |archive-date=11 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260211124614/https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/de/services-information/gemini-cooperation.html |url-status=live }} In January 2026, the complete takeover of the Florida International Terminal in [[Port Everglades]] by Rotterdam-based Hapag Lloyd subsidiary Hanseatic Global Terminals was announced. The company had already held a stake in the port since 2023.{{Cite web |title=Schifffahrt: Hapag-Lloyd expandiert in den USA - WELT |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/hamburg/article69622ec9b06bc41b8461c7b7/schifffahrt-hapag-lloyd-expandiert-in-den-usa.html |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=DIE WELT |language=de |archive-date=10 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260110115529/https://www.welt.de/regionales/hamburg/article69622ec9b06bc41b8461c7b7/schifffahrt-hapag-lloyd-expandiert-in-den-usa.html |url-status=live }} In February 2026 Hapag-Lloyd announced its acquisition of Israeli shipping company [[ZIM (shipping company)|ZIM]], for $4.2 billion.{{Cite news |date=2026-02-16 |title=Hapag-Lloyd, FIMI sign $4.2b ZIM acquisition deal |url=https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-hapag-lloyd-fimi-sign-42b-zim-acquisition-deal-1001535167 |access-date=2026-02-16 |work=Globes |language=en |archive-date=16 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260216170944/https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-hapag-lloyd-fimi-sign-42b-zim-acquisition-deal-1001535167 |url-status=live }} ==Corporate affairs== === Business trends === In the 2024 financial year, Hapag-Lloyd generated revenue of €19.1 billion. |- |[[Public Investment Fund]] |{{SAU}} |10.2% |} == Mergers and acquisitions == ===CP Ships Limited=== On 21 August 2005, TUI AG agreed to acquire the Canadian business [[CP Ships|CP Ships Limited]] for [[Euro|€]]1.7 billion ([[U.S. Dollar|US]]$2.0 billion) in cash. The deal, which was approved by the boards of both CP Ships, TUI, and the shareholders, was a success, and made the combined fleet the fifth-largest by capacity in the worldwide container shipping market.{{Cite news |last=Bienk |first=Kirsten |date=2005-08-22 |title=TUI Offers To Buy CP Ships |work=money.cnn.com |url=https://money.cnn.com/2005/08/22/news/international/news_snap.dj/index.htm |access-date=2022-05-15 |archive-date=15 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220515065130/https://money.cnn.com/2005/08/22/news/international/news_snap.dj/index.htm |url-status=dead}}{{Cite news |last=Singer |first=Jason |date=2005-08-20 |title=Germany's TUI to Acquire CP Ships in $2 Billion Deal |language=en-US |work=Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB112460985328918934 |access-date=2022-05-15 |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=15 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220515065129/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB112460985328918934 |url-status=live}}[[File:Colombo.Express.wmt.jpg|thumb|right|The ''[[Colombo Express]]'', 8600 TEU container ship owned and operated by Hapag-Lloyd]] ===Hamburg Süd=== In late 2012, Hapag-Lloyd announced it was considering the possibility of a merger with its smaller compatriot [[Hamburg Süd]]. The merger plans were scotched when Hamburg Süd's [[Dr. Oetker|shareholders and owners]] did not reach an agreement with the Hapag-Lloyd stakeholders.{{Cite news |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-hapag-lloyd-merger-idUKBRE92N0LE20130324 |title=Hapag-Lloyd merger with Hamburg-Sued called off |newspaper=Reuters |date=March 24, 2013 |via=uk.reuters.com |access-date=22 September 2019 |archive-date=22 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190922104011/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-hapag-lloyd-merger-idUKBRE92N0LE20130324 |url-status=dead}} After this event, Hamburg Süd remained a private, independent company until December 2016, when the [[Maersk Line|container transport division of Danish logistics and energy company]] [[Maersk]], announced it would purchase Hamburg Süd.{{Cite web |url=https://www.dw.com/en/oetker-group-sells-shipping-business-to-maersk/a-36600635 |title=Oetker group sells shipping business to Maersk | DW | 01.12.2016 |website=DW.COM |access-date=22 September 2019 |archive-date=8 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108100832/https://www.dw.com/en/oetker-group-sells-shipping-business-to-maersk/a-36600635 |url-status=live}} ===Compañía Sud Americana de Vapores (CSAV)=== In 2014, Hapag-Lloyd took over the container business of Chile's Compañía Sud Americana de Vapores SA ([[CSAV]]), with the latter becoming a major shareholder of Hapag-Lloyd. This made Hapag-Lloyd the fourth-largest container-shipping company in the world at the time.{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/2014/12/02/idUSFWN0TM00M20141202l |title=Regulators clear way for merger of Hapag-Lloyd and Vapores |work=[[Reuters]] |date=2 December 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924211117/http://www.reuters.com/article/2014/12/02/idUSFWN0TM00M20141202l |archive-date=24 September 2015}}"[http://www.handyshippingguide.com/shipping-news/approval-for-worlds-fourth-largest-container-shipping-line-granted_6006 Approval for World's Fourth Largest Container Shipping Line Granted] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028120712/https://handyshippingguide.com/shipping-news/approval-for-worlds-fourth-largest-container-shipping-line-granted_6006 |date=28 October 2020 }}" ''Handy Shipping Guide'', 2 December 2014. Accessed: 12 December 2014 ===United Arab Shipping Company (UASC)=== In April 2016, Hapag-Lloyd announced it was in merger talks with the United Arab Shipping Company (UASC). The merger was agreed upon later in 2016, and the integration between the two companies was completed in 2017. At the time of the merger, UASC was reported to be the world's 10th largest liner shipping company, with a fleet of 56 ships and a market share of 2.7 percent.{{Cite book |url=http://unctad.org/en/PublicationsLibrary/rmt2017_en.pdf |title=Review of Maritime Transport 2017 |publisher=United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) |year=2017 |isbn=978-92-1-362808-9 |editor-last=Barki |editor-first=Deniz |location=New York |pages=30 |quote=The Review of Maritime Transport 2017 covers data and events from January 2016 until June 2017. (p. viii) |editor-last2=Délèze-Black |editor-first2=Lucy |access-date=16 March 2018 |archive-date=6 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806175000/https://unctad.org/en/PublicationsLibrary/rmt2017_en.pdf |url-status=live}} As a result of the merger, Hapag-Lloyd strengthened its position as the world's fifth-largest container transporter in terms of vessel capacity, ahead of Taiwan's [[Evergreen Marine|Evergreen Line]]. As a result of the merger, the former shareholders of UASC would become the largest shareholder in the new entity, whilst Hapag-Lloyd would absorb all operations and assets of UASC.{{cite news |url=https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/press_and_media/press_release_page_48052.html |title=Talks between Hapag-Lloyd and United Arab Shipping Company |date=21 April 2016 |access-date=26 May 2016 |archive-date=26 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160526191101/https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/press_and_media/press_release_page_48052.html |url-status=live}} [[File:UASC Al Abdali berthed at SECH (Genoa).JPG|thumb|UASC's ''Al Abdali'']] Historically United Arab Shipping Company was jointly established in July 1976 by the six shareholding governments of the Arab states of the Gulf ([[Bahrain]], [[Iraq]], [[Kuwait]], [[Qatar]], [[Saudi Arabia]] and [[UAE]]).{{Cite web |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/480252/united-arab-shipping-joins-the-frontline-as-other-shipping-companies-retreat/ |title=United Arab Shipping joins the frontline as other shipping companies retreat |date=December 16, 2012 |website=The Express Tribune |access-date=23 October 2018 |archive-date=23 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023123420/https://tribune.com.pk/story/480252/united-arab-shipping-joins-the-frontline-as-other-shipping-companies-retreat/ |url-status=live}} Originally based in Kuwait, its corporate headquarters then moved to Dubai during the Iraqi conflict, and only some departments were moved back after the war.{{Cite web |url=https://www.joc.com/maritime-news/uasc-moving-back-kuwait-some-divisions-stay-dubai_19920630.html,%20/maritime-news/uasc-moving-back-kuwait-some-divisions-stay-dubai_19920630.html |title=UASC MOVING BACK TO KUWAIT SOME DIVISIONS TO STAY IN DUBAI |date=June 30, 1992 |website=www.joc.com |access-date=22 September 2019 |archive-date=15 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220515065135/https://www.joc.com/search404 |url-status=live}} The UASC fleet operated more than 45 services, connecting the [[Middle East]] to [[Europe]], the Mediterranean, Indian Sub-continent, [[Far East]], [[West Africa]] and the Americas.{{Cite web |url=https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/content/dam/website/downloads/pdf/HLAG_Investor_Presentation_Closing__.pdf |title=Hapag-Lloyd Investor Presentation |access-date=6 December 2019 |archive-date=6 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206191611/https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/content/dam/website/downloads/pdf/HLAG_Investor_Presentation_Closing__.pdf |url-status=live}} Its network covered over 220 ports, offering containerized and conventional cargo shipping by a fleet of 58 owned and chartered vessels.{{cite web |url=https://shippingwatch.com/carriers/article5886741.ece, |title=UASC signs USD 2.5 bln deal with Hyundai |date=30 August 2013 |publisher=Shipping Watch |access-date=21 September 2019 |archive-date=15 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220515065130/https://shippingwatch.com/carriers/article5886741.ece, |url-status=live}} On 29 June 2016, UASC's six shareholding states voted unanimously to approve the proposed merger. The deal gave a relative valuation of the two businesses at 72 percent for Hapag-Lloyd and 28 percent for UASC. At the time of the merger, UASC was 51 percent owned by Qatar and 35 percent owned by Saudi Arabia government, with the remainder held by other Arab states.{{Cite web |url=https://container-mag.com/2016/07/01/uasc-and-hapag-lloyds-merger-progresses/ |title=UASC and Hapag-Lloyd's merger progresses |first=Joe |last=Lo |date=July 1, 2016 |access-date=23 October 2018 |archive-date=23 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023120237/https://container-mag.com/2016/07/01/uasc-and-hapag-lloyds-merger-progresses/ |url-status=live}} ===NileDutch Transport & Shipping=== In March 2021, Hapag-Lloyd announced the acquisition of Nile Dutch Investments B.V., a leading container service provider to and from West Africa.{{Cite web |url=https://www.niledutch.com/en/news-media/posts/2021/march/hapag-lloyd-acquires-africa-specialist-niledutch/ |title=Hapag-Lloyd acquires Africa specialist NileDutch |access-date=22 March 2021 |archive-date=17 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210317211218/https://www.niledutch.com/en/news-media/posts/2021/march/hapag-lloyd-acquires-africa-specialist-niledutch/ |url-status=live}} The transaction was effectively closed on 8 July 2021.{{Cite web |title=Hapag-Lloyd acquires Africa carrier NileDutch - Hapag-Lloyd |url=https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2021/07/07.html |access-date=2021-09-24 |website=www.hapag-lloyd.com |date=8 July 2021 |language=en |archive-date=24 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924164257/https://www.hapag-lloyd.com/en/company/press/releases/2021/07/07.html |url-status=live}} === Deutsche Afrika-Linien === On 1 June 2022, Hapag-Lloyd closed the acquisition of the container liner business of German carrier [[Deutsche Afrika-Linien/John T. extract: Hapag-Lloyd AG (German pronunciation: [ˈhaːpak ˌlɔɪ̯t]) is a German international shipping and container transportation company, the 5th-largest in the world by total TEU capacity. It was formed in 1970 through a merger of two German maritime transportation companies.
